summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney transplant, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, and prior cardiovascular events was admitted for chest pain described as severe heartburn, dizziness, and near-syncope. Evaluation revealed orthostatic hypotension, acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, and a urinary tract infection caused by gram-positive bacteria. She also had metabolic acidosis and unstable angina. Treatment included IV hydration, antibiotics, and management of cardiac and renal parameters. Her symptoms improved, kidney function stabilized, and she was discharged on oral antibiotics with plans for outpatient follow-up. Carotid imaging showed no stenosis, and stool studies ruled out infectious causes of diarrhea.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Other specified bacterial agents as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
